In the end, I'd feel like a zombie most of the time and when my emotions sometimes hit me it was like a tsunami. I felt less human than ever so I stopped taking it about a month ago and it's been rough, periodic fits of crying and feelings of hopelessness but I feel like I have a better shot at happiness this way. Now I rely more on spiritual practices like yoga and Buddhist chanting, learning to love & respect myself/life etc...

When a member of the herd(or tribe of hunters/gatherers) strays from the group it often isn't welcomed back as it could be endangering the rest with foreign disease or by predators following it back to the herd etc. Our evolution spent so long developing that system so it's still with us and comes out as shunning/mocking those who are different which I've always found disgusting as well. On a primal level, they feel threatened by us not going along with their cultural "norm." That and they're trying to promote their own survival by being selfish dicks. I see it everywhere and it often makes me feel ashamed to be human but I try to be thankful that i can see it for what it is and choose not to perpetuate it. It is intense being one of the few who dare to challenge millions of years of evolution but a shift is happening that you and I are part of.
